problem.headline: Regulators Demand Transparency.
problem.subtitle: Transparency obligations and commercial confidentiality pull in opposite directions. PSI addresses the gap between them.
problem.card1Desc: The EU AI Act requires full auditability of AI decision-making. Articles 11–15 demand technical documentation, logging, and human oversight.
problem.card2Desc: Model weights are commercially sensitive. Publishing them is rarely acceptable to their owners, so disclosure alone is not a workable route to transparency.
problem.card3Desc: Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning can prove compliance without disclosure — but generating a ZK proof for every AI output is economically impossible at scale.
problem.card4Desc: Create integrity evidence without publishing model weights. This can support a compliance programme but does not replace legal, organisational or technical assessment.

solution.headline: Proof of Stateful Integrity
solution.subtitle: An experimental evidence architecture for recording claims, challenges and cryptographic verification results.
solution.feat1Desc: Assume compliant until challenged. Like optimistic rollups in blockchain — your AI outputs are 'innocent until proven guilty.'
solution.feat2Desc: Generate additional technical evidence when an output is challenged. Performance and cost depend on the proof and workload.
solution.feat3Desc: AI decision claims can be logged with SHA-256 hash chains so later modification is detectable when checkpoints are retained.
solution.feat4Desc: Rule-based screening can flag potential Annex III categories for qualified review; it is not a legal classification.
solution.feat5Desc: Generate draft documentation and evidence exports for review. Outputs require factual and legal validation.
solution.feat6Desc: Designed for future Zero-Knowledge integration. As ZK technology matures, PSI seamlessly upgrades from optimistic to full ZK verification.

faq.headline: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is Proof of Stateful Integrity (PSI)?
faq.a1: PSI is an evidence architecture that records declared context, hashes, signatures and challenge results. Experimental ZK components can add selective proofs, but the protocol does not assume or certify legal compliance.
faq.q2: How is this different from traditional ZKML?
faq.a2: ZKML performance and cost vary by model, circuit and hardware. PSI separates routine signed logging from optional challenge evidence instead of claiming that every output has a full model-execution proof.
faq.q3: What is the EU AI Act enforcement date?
faq.a3: The Act uses a phased application timeline. Article 50 became applicable on 2 August 2026; penalty tiers depend on the breached provision and entity.
faq.q4: Do I need to disclose my model weights?
faq.a4: Not for basic receipt verification. Experimental selective-proof features may reduce disclosure, but organisations must assess what documentation regulators and counterparties require.
faq.q5: What EU AI Act articles does PSI cover?
faq.a5: PSI provides technical evidence controls that may support selected workflows under Articles 11–15 and 50. It does not provide automatic legal coverage or conformity.
